name: Armenian (Western)
variety: Standard Western Armenian of the diaspora, as spoken in Beirut, in the classical (Mashtotsian) orthography. There is no monolingual community; the realisation of the plosives depends on the majority language of the speaker's country.
sources: Seyfarth, Scott, Dolatian, Hossep, Guekguezian, Peter, Kelly, Niamh & Toparlak, Tabita (2024). Armenian (Yerevan Eastern Armenian and Beirut Western Armenian). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 54(1): 445-478.
Kelly, Niamh E. & Keshishian, Lara (2021). Voicing patterns in stops among heritage speakers of Western Armenian in Lebanon and the US. Nordic Journal of Linguistics 44: 103-129.
Kelly, Niamh E. & Keshishian, Lara (2019). The voicing contrast in stops and affricates in the Western Armenian of Lebanon. Proceedings of Interspeech 2019: 1721-1725.
Toparlak, Tabita (2019). Etudes phonétiques en arménien. Mémoire de master, Université Paris III Sorbonne Nouvelle. Formant values as published in Seyfarth et al. (2024).
Toparlak, Tabita & Dolatian, Hossep (2022). Intonation and focus marking in Western Armenian. Proceedings of the 4th Conference on Central Asian Languages and Linguistics (ConCALL-4): 81-94.

Athanasopoulou, Angeliki, Vogel, Irene & Dolatian, Hossep (2017). Acoustic properties of canonical and non-canonical stress in French, Turkish, Armenian and Brazilian Portuguese. Proceedings of Interspeech 2017: 1398-1402.
Vaux, Bert (1998). The Phonology of Armenian. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
Fairbanks, Gordon H. (1948). Phonology and morphology of modern spoken West Armenian. PhD dissertation, University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Baronian, Luc (2017). Two problems in Armenian phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 11(8).

vowel_formants.speaker: adult male (mean of three male speakers from Beirut, aged 21-40, words in sentences and in isolation)
vowel_formants.source: Toparlak 2019, as tabulated in Seyfarth et al. 2024, Table 2
vowel_formants.notes: Arrays are F1, F2, F3 in Hz, rounded to 10 Hz by the source. Female means (Table 1): i 350 2550 3330, e 500 2200 3120, ə 480 1650 3020, ɑ 720 1510 2990, o 450 1100 2870, u 360 1020 2990. No values are published for [ʏ]. The schwa is closer than in Yerevan.

contrasts: two-way laryngeal contrast in plosives and affricates: voiced against voiceless (traditionally described as aspirated)

the Western voiced series answers to the Eastern voiceless unaspirated series, and the Western voiceless series to both the Eastern voiced and the Eastern aspirated series: Eastern [pɑɾ] 'dance' is Western [bɑɾ], Eastern [bɑr] 'word' is Western [pʰɑɾ]
one rhotic, the tap /ɾ/: the trill of Eastern Armenian has merged with it
dental against postalveolar affricates, two of each
six vowels as in Eastern Armenian; a front rounded [ʏ] for written իւ varies with [ju], and [œ] for written էօ is found in a few loanwords and names
no vowel length and no gemination
allophony: the voiceless plosives are aspirated for speakers in North America and for the Beirut speaker of the Journal of the IPA illustration, but have a short lag of about 20 ms, like the voiceless stops of Lebanese Arabic, for speakers living in Lebanon
the voiced plosives have voicing through the closure between vowels; at the start of an utterance they are often voiceless unaspirated
the voiceless plosives are unaspirated next to a voiceless sibilant; the first of two plosives is often unaspirated; two identical voiceless plosives give one long aspirated plosive
the voiceless affricates are unaspirated [ts tʃ] in the Beirut variety
devoicing in obstruent clusters works in both directions: a voiced obstruent is devoiced before and after a voiceless one
/ɾ/ is often spirantised in the coda; between vowels it is a tap or approximant
/ʁ/ varies between a fricative and an approximant; /χ/ is roughly velar and /ʁ/ roughly uvular for some speakers
/n/ takes the place of a following obstruent: [suŋɡ] 'mushroom'
the schwa is higher than in Eastern Armenian, close to [ə̝]
in the classical orthography word-initial յ is [h] and word-final յ after ա or ո is silent; ոյ is [uj]; իւ is [ʏ] or [ju]
phonotactics: written consonant clusters are broken by an unwritten schwa, as in Eastern Armenian
word-initial sibilant plus stop always takes a prothetic schwa in citation forms
two-consonant codas with falling sonority need no schwa
stem-final /kʰ/ is added to any coda without schwa: [bɑɾdkʰ] 'debt'
nasal plus obstruent clusters are homorganic
vowel hiatus is repaired mostly by an inserted [j]

stress.type: fixed final, with a few morphological exceptions
stress.rule: Stress falls on the last syllable unless its vowel is schwa, in which case it falls on the last full vowel; clitics are unstressed; some verb forms are stressed on the theme vowel before the ending and some negative forms on the first syllable.
stress.cues: mean F0 and F0 excursion (Athanasopoulou, Vogel & Dolatian 2017); for the Beirut speaker of the Journal of the IPA illustration also longer duration and a more peripheral vowel

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: only schwa is reduced or dropped; high vowels alternate with schwa or zero when derivation moves the stress

length.notes: No length contrast. Two identical voiceless plosives across a morpheme boundary are spoken as one long plosive.

voice_onset_time_ms.source: Kelly & Keshishian 2021, speakers living in Lebanon, coronal stops in real words in a carrier sentence
voice_onset_time_ms.notes: In nonce words the same group had -80.9 ms for the voiced stop and 20.6 ms for the voiceless one (of which 14.5 ms aspiration). Speakers in the United States had 78.8 ms for the voiceless stop and -12.4 ms, with great variation, for the voiced one. A synthesiser aiming at the traditional description should use the aspirated value.

intonation.declarative: subject, object, verb order; each constituent before the nucleus ends in a rise, the peaks step down, the nuclear accent is on the element before the verb and the verb is deaccented; low final boundary
intonation.yes_no_question: word order of a statement with a final rise on the verb to a high boundary
intonation.wh_question: rise on the question word, the rest deaccented, and a final rise to a high boundary (Eastern Armenian ends low)
intonation.continuation: high target at the right edge of each non-final constituent
intonation.accent_shape: rise to a high target on the final, stressed syllable of the word
intonation.notes: After Toparlak (2019) and Toparlak & Dolatian (2022) as reported by Seyfarth et al. (2024).

problems: The conditional rules for Western Armenian in hy_rules (marked ?1) do not fire with this voice, although the voice file sets dictrules 1 (tested with the 1.53 build; apparently because tr_languages.c has no entry for hyw, so that Armenian script is handed to the hy translator). So the classical spelling is misread: word-initial յ stays [j] (Յակոբ gives [jaɡopʰ] for [hɑɡop]), ոյ stays [oj] (լոյս gives [lojs] for [lujs]) and final silent յ is pronounced (տղայ gives [dəʀaɪ] for [dəˈʁɑ]).
ռ and ր remain two sounds (trill R and the approximant r); Western Armenian has a single tap.
ր is the base phoneme r, an approximant of the English type before vowels, and ղ is the uvular trill r" instead of the fricative [ʁ].
No devoicing in obstruent clusters and no loss of aspiration next to sibilants.
The default intonation tunes are used: question-word questions do not end in a rise.
good: the Western consonant shift is applied by phoneme replacement in the voice file: written բ գ դ ձ ջ are voiceless aspirated and written պ կ տ ծ ճ are voiced
stress is final and never falls on schwa
front rounded vowels for written իւ and էօ exist in the phoneme table
the unwritten schwa is inserted as for Eastern Armenian, and always before initial sibilant plus stop, which suits Western Armenian

notes: The voice shares the dictionary and phoneme table of Eastern Armenian; apart from the consonant replacement it speaks Western spelling with Eastern rules.
